results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 27 outline summaries match the controlling ideas of their aligned spec paragraphs, in spec order. Note (not a failure): the Established list (p23) recaps incident reviews, which the spec's controlling idea does not name, and omits 'measured by four measures', which it does.

Introduction ¶2 (marked two_ideas: thesis / roadmap) carries exactly what the spec places in p02, the thesis statement and the roadmap of a lead paragraph; Checklist ¶2 (marked two_ideas: callback / hand-off) is the declared hand-off paragraph whose transition carries over the declined proposal. Neither is a second controlling idea.

The outliner needed two summaries, and the paragraph does two jobs: it reports what the research associates with performance (evidence for team ownership) and it defines the four delivery measures (set-up for later sections), with two sourcing asides between them. Both flow readers (A5, B4, each rated b) re-read it to find its point. The spec's controlling idea for p07 joins the same two ideas with 'and', so the draft follows the spec.

results.quote: The research measures delivery with four measures: lead time for a change, deployment frequency, **change failure rate** (the share of releases that need a fix or a return to the previous version right away) and **time to restore** (how long recovery takes).

results.finding: Every term on the does_not_know list is defined at or before first use in the body: escaped defect and enabling team (principles ¶1), change failure rate and time to restore (principles ¶3), delivery path (path ¶1), incident review (builds-it ¶2), launch readiness (launch ¶1), separation of duties (opposing view ¶1). On-call rotation, verification, runbook and service-level objectives are glossed in a clause. Not recorded as a failure: 'Corvane's fifth stage' (reader B, item B6, rated b, one reader) belongs to the book's Corvane frame.
The introduction opens on a specific anecdote (the outage and the proposal), bridges to the reader's own meeting and states a disputable thesis; none of the weak patterns.

The conclusion sorts what holds by how settled it is, gives the synthesis, a course of action and a hand-off; it does not open with 'in conclusion', add a subtopic, hold body evidence or end on a rephrased thesis alone.

The synthesis (quality and reliability as one loop of check, pager and review, cut by a gate held by others) is stated in the author's synthesis and in no single section; the so-what is the checklist lead: ask which check, which pager and which review were missing, and judge by change failure rate, time to restore and escaped defects.

The closing paragraph returns to the thirteen hours of May 2026 and the QA team of ten, says the proposal was declined and why a sign-off would have supplied neither the way back nor the pager, with the independent look coming from a second engineer.

The intro reader predicted all eight sections in the spec's order (night and proposal, placements, the three patterns, the objection, the decision, AI) and the tone. One miss, not on the roadmap: it expected little external citation, while the chapter leans on DORA, Larson and Matsudaira.

The cold reader's answer contains every element of the expected answer: the gate is a queue and a hand-off and moves ownership from the teams; instead keep ownership in the teams, put the checks in one delivery path, use quality engineers as an enabling team, and judge by change failure rate, time to restore and escaped defects. It also adds the condition for an outside check.

The AI section carries three labeled claims (Proven: DORA 2024; Emerging: the author's observation, dated and marked as not a measurement; Speculative: independence applied to agents, with what would confirm it) and points to [[agentic-delivery]] for the full argument.

Named sources carry book and concept (Larson, An Elegant Puzzle, gatekeeping; Larson, The Engineering Executive's Primer, the weekly review; DORA's guides and the 2019 and 2024 reports; Matsudaira through the author's record), the reliance on DORA's guides in place of notes on Accelerate is declared, and the author's extensions are marked ('the costs in the third column are my reading', 'The test of a review, which is mine', 'I offer this as a recommendation', the four signs and the application to agents 'are mine'). Notes, not failures: 'Larson writes' in the on-call paragraph relies on the book named a section earlier; rules two and three of the incident review carry no source and no 'mine'.

Each pattern names a user and outcome measures: checks in the path (the team making a change; change failure rate, wait before release), enabling specialists (the team being helped; checks maintained alone a quarter later, escaped defects), on-call (the owning team; time to restore, pages per shift), incident review (teams that run services; repeat-cause incidents, actions closed within a month), launch readiness (the launching team and whoever is on call; first-month incidents, wait between ready and launched).
